lead: The historic heart of the district: Carrer Gran, the former Fabra i Coats factory and village life.
text: It was an independent municipality with more than a thousand years of documented history, annexed to Barcelona on 20 April 1897. Its origin is agricultural: around the neo-Gothic church of Sant Andreu, from 1881, grew Carrer Gran, an old Roman road from which the other streets branch off, and in 1640 the reapers who sparked the Corpus de Sang uprising set out from its parish.

Today it has 59,330 inhabitants in 1.87 km², with a very active neighbourhood life, above all in sport, with clubs such as UE Sant Andreu, and local shops that stretch as far as Passeig de Fabra i Puig. The former Fabra i Coats factory was reclaimed in 1995 as a cultural centre and library, and the Casa Bloc, from the 1930s, is one of the finest examples of rationalist housing in the city.
housing: Low-rise houses in the old centre and blocks of flats from different periods.
